clue.text: Small present for author

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
the present moment is now

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a modest gift for a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but is the time sense: now. C. P. Snow was the English novelist of the Strangers and Brothers series.
explanation.definitionFit: C. P. Snow was a British novelist and scientist, so his surname stands for a writer.

clue.text: See 24 across
Person with burning desire to get rid of parent?

definitions.text: Person with burning desire to get rid of parent?

parts.words: Person with burning desire to get rid of parent?
parts.note: read as fire (sack, get rid of) plus a word for a parent, one who brings up a child; literally, someone who longs to start fires

explanation.surface: A child who wants to be rid of a mother or father.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the split reading: to fire is to dismiss, and a raiser is one who rears children.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsonist is someone with a burning urge, literally, to set things alight.

clue.text: Causes of division in western borders

parts.note: borders are edges

explanation.surface: Something splitting communities along the frontiers of the West.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge is driven in to split wood, and figuratively anything that divides people.

clue.text: Put down like overlapping sleeping places

parts.note: as means like, in the sense 'as good as'

indicators.note: the two words for beds share one letter where they meet, so that letter is counted only once

parts.note: a crib is a baby's bed
a bed is a place to sleep
the shared letter where the two words overlap

explanation.surface: Bunks arranged so that one overlaps another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlapping' means the two sleeping-place words share the letter where one ends and the next begins, so it is written once.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something down to a cause is to attribute it, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Pressing a variety of rose

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the flower's letters appear in another arrangement

explanation.surface: Flattening a particular cultivar of a garden flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' suggests flower-pressing but is the adjective for urgent or painful.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressing or painful matter is one that hurts or rankles, as in a touchy point.

clue.text: Foreign citizen contributing all our articles about part of UK

indicators.note: the articles stand around the region's abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: English has only three articles: a, the and an
NI is Northern Ireland, one part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A journalist from abroad contributes pieces about a British region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks journalistic but means the grammatical ones; 'about' wraps them round the region's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Athens is a foreigner from a British viewpoint, a native of the Greek capital.

clue.text: Place for eating dog's dinner

definitions.meaning: a military dining hall, the officers' version being well known
British slang for a muddle or shambles

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an armed forces dining room and, informally, a chaotic jumble.

clue.text: Unpleasant quality of new wine going to head

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Fresh wine that goes straight to the head has an unpleasant effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is the geographical sense, a promontory, not the head that wine goes to.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastiness is the abstract noun for being unpleasant or spiteful.

clue.text: See 13
A little bit European, or totally so?

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in 'not a whit'

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is slightly European or wholly so.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is itself a little bit plus European; 'or totally so?' asks for a word meaning of wholly European descent.
explanation.definitionFit: As a racial label, the colour word describes people of entirely European ancestry.

clue.text: Awfully enraged queen's doomed 2, 5 and 7 trying to make 11 16 19 across

definitions.text: doomed 2, 5 and 7 trying to make 11 16 19 across

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: R is Regina, the queen, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: An angry queen condemns the three card-men trying to recolour her flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: In Alice in Wonderland the playing cards Two, Five and Seven paint the white roses red; the Queen of Hearts orders their heads off.
explanation.definitionFit: The three cards in Lewis Carroll's story were employed tending the Queen's rose garden.

clue.text: Arguments about backing untried and gentle warrior in conflict

indicators.note: the arguments word goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: theses are propositions put forward in argument

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for untried is turned round

parts.note: raw means inexperienced, untried
soft means gentle
a hero is a brave warrior

explanation.surface: Disputes over supporting an inexperienced, mild-mannered fighter in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the word for untried; 'about' wraps the arguments word round all three pieces. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth-century English civil wars between York and Lancaster were a dynastic conflict.

clue.text: River bank split by front of barge

indicators.note: the word for bank is broken open with a letter set inside it

parts.note: a bank of seats is a tier, a row

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A riverbank divided by the bow of a passing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests a riverside but means a row or tier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the river flowing through Rome.

clue.text: More muscular fellow that is getting stuck into drink

indicators.note: the pieces are lodged inside the drink, so they sit within it

parts.note: beer is a drink
ie is id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A man tucking into his pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting stuck into' looks like someone eagerly drinking, but it places the two short pieces inside the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefy means brawny and well-built, so the comparative means more brawny.

clue.text: Put together royalty in two parts for humorous author

parts.note: Edward is the name of several English kings
Lear is Shakespeare's legendary king of Britain

explanation.surface: Assembling a royal figure from two pieces to make a comic writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put together' and 'in two parts' signal two king names placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear was the Victorian writer of nonsense verse and limericks, a humorous author.

clue.text: See 13 across
Is passionate — his darling resembles a 19 21 rearranged

definitions.meaning: to be aflame with love or desire
red rose-red rearranged gives 'red, red rose', which the Scottish poet's love is like in his famous song

explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns, Scotland's national poet, wrote 'O my Luve is like a red, red rose'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means is aflame with feeling, and the surname is Scotland's best-known poet.

clue.text: Determined to produce notes on stringed instrument

parts.note: re and so are notes of the sol-fa scale
a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Resolved to make music on a lute.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolute means firmly decided, steadfast in purpose.

clue.text: Like diamonds or rubies

parts.note: diamonds here is the card suit, coloured the same as rubies, so both share a colour

explanation.walkthrough: Diamonds suggests gems, which are colourless; read it as the playing-card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The diamond suit in cards and the ruby gemstone are both of this colour.

clue.text: Cardinal, say, with parrots or other birds

parts.note: cardinal is a deep scarlet shade, an example of a colour
Poll or Polly is a stock name for a parrot

explanation.surface: A cardinal bird keeps company with parrots and other species.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal and parrots look like birds, and the cardinal is one, but here it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Redpolls are small finches, birds other than the cardinal and parrots mentioned.

clue.text: 11 and parts of 21 one spotted in all directions

indicators.note: the letter is seen inside the compass letters, placed within them

parts.note: W, N, E and S are the four compass points
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single item spotted wherever one looks.
explanation.walkthrough: White, rose and red, from 11 and 21, are the three colours of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: White, rosé and red are the three kinds of wine, so the colours define the drinks.

clue.text: Like 28, sister of 1 11

definitions.meaning: the ancient city of 28 is called 'a ... city half as old as time' in Burgon's poem
in the Grimm tale, the girl with a pink name is sister of Snow-White

explanation.definitionFit: Petra's sandstone is described with this colour phrase, and it is the fairy-tale sister's name.

clue.text: Variety of red rose that's put at back of altar

definitions.text: that's put at back of altar

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the two words' letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A kind of red flower placed behind the altar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety' suggests a horticultural cultivar but signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen standing behind a church altar.

clue.text: Grey squirrel, for example — not red, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A grey squirrel is, strangely, not a red one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' could suggest odd letters; it signals an anagram. Britain's red squirrel has been displaced by the American grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Squirrels are gnawing mammals, so a grey squirrel is an example of the order.

clue.text: Argument about area being in the red, note

indicators.note: the area letter is placed inside the word for money owed

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A dispute over a region that is losing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a formal argument between opposing sides.

clue.text: Demolish a flat as dreadfully archaic, like 28

indicators.note: dreadfully means very badly, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Knocking down an apartment because it is terribly old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: Burgon's poem calls the city of 28 'a rose-red city half as old as time'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from Burgon's poem describes ancient Petra, so it means very old.

clue.text: Parts of body that'll grow into 16

definitions.meaning: the joints at the top of the legs
the fruits that form on the flowers of 16 after blooming

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the body's pelvic joints and the red fruit of the briar.

clue.text: Letters regularly lost by railways, unfortunately

indicators.note: every other letter is dropped, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: Railways regrettably lose letters on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the odd letters R, I, W, Y and keep the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an interjection expressing regret, used like 'sadly'.

clue.text: Shot in air near political campaigners

parts.note: a lob is a high looping shot in tennis
by means near, as in 'close by'

explanation.surface: A shot fired into the air close to protesters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire but is a tennis stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobby is a group campaigning to influence legislators.

clue.text: Get out under willow in cathedral city

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to bowl a batsman with a ball pitching under the bat, which is made of willow
the northern English city with its Minster

explanation.definitionFit: The verb is to dismiss with a full-length ball, and it is also a northern English cathedral city.

clue.text: Latin name for girl from ancient city

definitions.meaning: the feminine form of Peter, from the word for rock
the rock-cut Nabataean city in Jordan

explanation.definitionFit: It is a female forename and the rock-carved ancient city in Jordan.

clue.text: Demolished ancestral house, as opposed to 27

indicators.note: demolished means knocked down, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Knocking down the family seat, unlike the rival house.
explanation.walkthrough: The Houses of Lancaster and York fought the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal House of Lancaster was the red-rose rival dynasty to York.
